items.title: Anonymous / all-employee exposure
items.description: Identify spaces readable by anonymous users or by every logged-in employee. Sensitive content in these spaces is effectively public to the whole org (or the internet). Map which spaces have the widest audience so their content is prioritised for search.
items.examples:
List spaces with the anonymous-access permission enabled.
List spaces granted to the 'confluence-users' / all-employees group.
Record the audience size next to each space in the ledger.

items.title: External / guest account reach
items.description: Enumerate external, guest and contractor accounts and what spaces they can reach. Sensitive data visible to external accounts is a common oversharing failure. Confirm the audit's own auth context first: 'exposed to whom' depends on which user you are searching as.
items.examples:
List guest/external users and their space grants.
Search as a low-privilege / external account and diff the results against an admin view.
Note any sensitive space an external account can read.

items.title: Personal spaces oversharing
items.description: Personal spaces are frequently left open and used to stash credentials, tokens and drafts. Sweep personal spaces specifically rather than assuming they are private.
items.examples:
CQL: type = page AND space.type = personal
Search personal spaces for the secrets and PII dictionaries.
Flag any personal space with a broad audience.

items.title: Instance-wide secret sweep
items.description: Run instance-wide searches for credentials and machine secrets across all in-scope spaces. Cover passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys and connection strings. Log every query and every hit to the ledger; broaden terms rather than stopping early.
items.examples:
CQL/text: password, passwd, api_key, apikey, secret, token, Bearer, BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY, AKIA, xoxb-, connectionstring
Try synonyms, abbreviations, misspellings and other languages.
Record page URL + space + audience for each hit.

items.title: Instance-wide PII sweep
items.description: Search all in-scope spaces for personal and regulated data: employee records, salaries, home addresses, ID/passport numbers, customer data. Note the applicable sensitivity (GDPR/PII) and who can currently read it.
items.examples:
Text: salary, IBAN, passport, date of birth, employee ID, home address, personal data
Search HR / onboarding / finance spaces specifically.
Record the data category and audience per hit.

items.title: Instance-wide infrastructure / access sweep
items.description: Search for internal architecture, network topology, hostnames, and 'how to access X' runbooks that hand an attacker a map or a foothold. These are high value even without a raw credential.
items.examples:
Text: VPN, jump host, bastion, ssh, internal hostname patterns, 'how to access', runbook, admin, kubeconfig
Collect network diagrams and admin runbooks.
Note what each doc would give an attacker.

items.title: Search space for credentials/secrets
items.description: Search this space specifically for credentials and machine secrets using the full secrets dictionary. Space-scoped search catches hits the instance-wide sweep buried or ranked low. Do not finish until every secrets term has been tried against this space.
items.examples:
CQL: text ~ 'password' AND space = <KEY>
Walk the page tree; do not rely on search ranking alone.
Record each hit with page URL and the surrounding context.

items.title: Search space for PII / regulated data
items.description: Search this space for personal and regulated data using the PII dictionary. Prioritise HR, finance, onboarding and customer spaces, but check every in-scope space.
items.examples:
CQL: text ~ 'salary' AND space = <KEY>
Open tables and exported reports embedded in pages.
Record data category and audience per hit.

items.title: Search space for infra / access docs
items.description: Search this space for network diagrams, hostnames, credentials-to-systems runbooks and access instructions. Capture anything that would help an attacker move laterally.
items.examples:
CQL: text ~ 'VPN' OR text ~ 'runbook' AND space = <KEY>
Review any 'Onboarding' or 'IT' page trees in full.
Note the systems each doc references.

items.title: Review space attachments
items.description: Enumerate this space's attachments and inspect names and bodies for secrets and PII. Attachments are where real secrets hide: config files, key material, exported spreadsheets and diagrams.
items.examples:
CQL: type = attachment AND space = <KEY>
Flag names: .env, .pem, .pfx, id_rsa, .kubeconfig, .sql, .xlsx, .pcap, backup
Download and grep suspicious files for keys/PII.

items.title: Review space permissions vs. content
items.description: Compare this space's audience against the sensitivity of what it holds. A password in a space two admins can read is a different severity than one in an all-company space. Record the audience so findings can be scored correctly.
items.examples:
List the groups/users granted read on the space.
Note whether anonymous or all-employees can read it.
Set severity context: sensitivity x audience size.

items.title: Check comments and old page versions
items.description: Sensitive data often lives in page comments or in older versions that were 'redacted' in the current view but remain in history. Check comments and the version history of high-value pages in this space.
items.examples:
Read comments on credential/runbook pages.
Open page history and diff older revisions for removed secrets.
Record any secret still retrievable from history.
